title: Developer velocity quick-pitch + PAYG pricing drafts
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a concise messaging brief + experiment plan for a developer-first hosted API landing/quickstart and two PAYG pricing language variants. Intended audience: developer onboarding emails, docs hero copy, quickstart snippets in SDK guides, and a small A/B test on the sign-up funnel.

Context / problem we solve (working phrasing):
- Developers want to move from prototype to production without surprises: fast integration, predictable latency, and clear unit economics.
- Existing messaging in market either focuses on model access or enterprise SLAs — we can win on the middle ground: easy to start + production-grade performance you can trust.

Core developer-first value props (short lines for hero + bullets):
1) Ship in minutes: 5-line SDKs, Postman collection, and a sample app that returns from prod-quality models.
2) Predictable performance at low friction: transparent per-token economics, latency SLOs, and easy autoscaling controls.
3) Save by default: automatic batching & KV-prefix caching suggestions tailored to your prompts.
4) Same API when you grow: start on Hosted API, lift to Dedicated or Private without re-architecting.

Hero headline variants (A/B candidates):
A: "Build with LLMs that behave in production — fast SDKs, clear pricing, predictable latency."
B: "From prototype to production: integrate an inference API that scales and explains costs."
C (concise): "Ship LLM features faster — predictable performance, transparent pricing."

Supporting bullets (for hero subtext):
- Five-minute quickstart, ready-to-run examples, and sample apps.
- Token-level cost breakdown in the console; recommendations to reduce spend by up to 3x.
- Streaming, function calls, and SDKs for JS/Python/Go out of the box.

Quickstart angles (developer paths to test):
1) "5-line Chat demo" — minimal JS snippet in hero, click-to-run in embedded sandbox. Measures: time-to-first-response, sign-ups that open SDK docs.
2) "Clone + run sample app" — GitHub repo that starts with a simple chat/agent example and an e2e docker-compose for local testing. Measures: repo clones, demo runs, API key usage.
3) "Postman + Playbook" — importable Postman collection + checklist for migrating prototype to prod (caching, batching, rate limits). Measures: collection imports, follow-up support requests.
4) "Migration path CTA" — short flow that explains how to move to Dedicated/Private when you hit thresholds. Measures: contacts for enterprise evals.

Pricing-language drafts (developer-friendly PAYG copy):
Variant 1 (Transparent unit economics — conservative):
- "Pay only for what you use — per-token pricing starting at $0.0009 / input token and $0.0018 / output token (example tiers). No commit, cancel anytime. Billing shows token-breakdown by route and model so you can optimize."
- Explicit bullets: free $100 trial credit, invoicing for teams, volume discounts at monthly commit.

Variant 2 (Developer-first tone — higher conversion test):
- "Start for free. Pay per call. See exact cost for every request in the console. We'll tell you how to cut your bill — automatic batching and cache suggestions, plus per-route cost alerts."
- Callout: "No surprises — tokens, latency, and recommendations visible in one place."

Edge-case wording for security-conscious customers:
- "Data not used to train models by default. Enterprise encryption and audit logging available for Dedicated/Private."

Competitive positioning notes (short hits vs common competitors):
- vs large cloud inference endpoints: Lead with developer UX + transparent per-token breakdown and model-performance benchmarks. Clouds win on infra scale; we win on hand-holding for inference optimizations and cost controls.
- vs API-first model providers: They focus on model breadth. We emphasize serving economics: latency SLOs, batching, and fallback model variants to keep apps online under load.
- vs inference runtimes/self-hosted: We sell a hosted on-ramp + same API if you later self-host with Dedicated/Private. Highlight "no lock-in" (same SDK + code paths).

Quick rebuttals / objections and suggested responses:
- "We can run this cheaper ourselves." -> "Maybe — but teams underestimate ops cost: kernel selection, batching logic, quantization, and observability. We reduce time-to-savings and risk with production tooling and rollback policies."
- "We need enterprise controls." -> "Hosted + Dedicated + Private options, with explicit migrations and audit logs. We can run a security and network review with solutions engineering."

Experimental messaging tests (metrics to capture):
- Primary conversion metrics: signups -> api-key created -> first successful API call -> paid conversion.
- Secondary: time to first-run, sample app clone, console cost-explore event.
- A/B test plan: Hero headline A/B (three variants), Pricing block A/B (Variant 1 vs Variant 2), Quickstart CTA A/B (Sandbox vs GitHub clone).

Suggested copy for product pages / docs (short snippets):
- Quickstart CTA: "Try a 5-line chat in your browser — no account required."
- Pricing CTA: "Start free with $100 credit, pay-as-you-go after. See live per-request cost in the console."

Landing page layout (high-level idea):
- Hero (headline + 3 bullets)
- 5-line quickstart with embedded example (click to run)
- Pricing snapshot (short PAYG + trial) + link to full pricing page
- Developer trust strip: SDKs, benchmarks, case study blurbs, and open-source sample apps
- Migration path block: "Grow into Dedicated or Private"

Ops & docs checklist (what product/engineering needs to ship for launch):
- Ready: 5-line SDK snippet for JS/Python/Go (examples in repo).
- Ready: sandbox runner in docs with rate-limited demo keys.
- Needed: landing pricing snippet + legal approval for trial terms. (Owner: Legal)
- Needed: console event to show per-request cost and expose recommendations. (Owner: Console team)
- Needed: Postman collection and a small "hardening checklist" doc for prototyping -> prod. (Owner: Developer Experience)

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Do we want to show explicit example price numbers on hero, or keep them off until pricing page? (Tradeoff: transparency vs complexity.)
- How aggressive should the cost-savings claims be (e.g., "up to 3x"): need an internal benchmark to justify.
- SLA language for hosted tier vs Dedicated — what exact latency SLOs can we commit to on hosted? (Ping SRE/serving-runtime.)

Next steps / proposed owners:
- Finalize A/B headlines + variants (Owner: Leah / Samir) — due EOD 2024-10-21.
- Implement 5-line snippet & embed sandbox (Owner: DevX / Marco) — prototype by 2024-11-05.
- Legal to sign off on trial terms + pricing copy (Owner: Finance/Legal) — target 2024-11-12.
- Instrument conversion funnel events in signup flow (Owner: Growth Analytics) — 2024-11-15.

Notes / scratchpad (informal):
- Short anecdote for comms: dev on call said: "We switched from vendor X because their comments on cost were opaque — we couldn't see which routes were racking up tokens." This supports per-request visibility play.
- TODO: draft sample onboarding email sequence (welcome -> quickstart -> cost tips -> migrate path).

End of brief.
